problem: Waypoint predictors used in VLN-CE are language-agnostic and often fail to generate waypoints at critical locations mentioned in the instruction, which limits overall navigation performance.
motivation: Waypoint-based VLN-CE methods abstract navigable locations to ease action prediction, but inaccurate waypoints cap their performance. The authors attribute this to the lack of language context in the predictor, so it misses waypoints for locations the instructions refer to.
key_idea: Condition the waypoint predictor on language by using a pre-trained navigation agent as the language encoder, and alternately train the agent and the predictor in a cycle so each improves the other.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that language-conditioned waypoints raise waypoint quality above all existing predictors and that the gap to the waypoint-based upper bound narrows by about 60%. The cycle training is motivated by the disparity between the language-encoder agent and the final navigation agent.
method: Agent-based language encoding: a pre-trained VLN-CE agent encodes the instruction (grounded with the environment) as language context for the waypoint predictor.
Language-conditioned waypoint predictor: trained on data collected with the same agent.
New navigation agent: trained using waypoints from the proposed predictor.
Cycle training: alternately trains the agent and the waypoint predictor to reduce the disparity between the language-encoder agent and the navigation agent.

setting.backbone: pre-trained VLN-CE agent as language encoder + waypoint predictor + navigation agent (details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: data collected with the pre-trained agent in VLN-CE environments (details not given in the abstract)
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE), not stated in the abstract

results: The abstract claims the waypoint predictor surpasses all existing ones. With better waypoints, the gap between waypoint-based methods and their upper bound narrows by about 60%. No specific metric values are given.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so specifics on data, metrics and baselines are unknown.
Training is more complex: it needs a pre-trained agent and alternating cycle training.
